codeReview.summary: The implementation correctly adds Tauri commands for proxy management (add_proxy, update_proxy, delete_proxy, get_proxies, clear_proxies, get_proxy_pool, update_proxy_pool_config, assign_domain_proxy, unassign_domain_proxy). All commands are properly registered in lib.rs and follow the existing codebase patterns. The worker added 16 unit tests that cover the core functionality, and all 85 backend tests pass. The implementation extends the existing Settings struct with a proxy_pool field using #[serde(default)] for backward compatibility with existing settings files.

issues.description: The add_proxy command directly modifies settings.proxy_pool without persisting to disk. While the proxy pool is stored in memory and will be persisted on the next save_settings call, there's no automatic persistence after proxy operations. This could lead to data loss if the app crashes before settings are saved. Consider adding auto-save or explicit save after proxy modifications.

Frontend hook makes an extra get_proxy_pool call after each proxy operation to refresh state. This is correct but creates an extra IPC round-trip. Consider having backend commands return the updated state to eliminate the extra call.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The Settings struct uses snake_case for field names (validation_mode, timeout_ms, proxy_pool) while nested structs like ProxyPool use camelCase via #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]. This mixed convention is consistent with existing code but may cause confusion for developers working across the boundary.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src-tauri/src/settings.rs:354-360 shows Settings with snake_case fields; src-tauri/src/settings.rs:200 shows ProxyPool with #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]

sharedStateObservations.observation: Tauri commands consistently return Result<T, String> for error handling, using String error messages. This pattern is followed across all proxy commands.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src-tauri/src/settings.rs:472-566 shows all proxy commands following Result<T, String> pattern

sharedStateObservations.observation: The #[serde(default)] attribute on proxy_pool field in Settings ensures backward compatibility when loading settings files from before this feature was added. This is a useful pattern for future settings migrations.

summary: PASS. The proxy-tauri-commands feature is well-implemented and meets all expected behaviors. The worker followed TDD principles, adding 16 comprehensive unit tests. All commands are properly registered and follow existing patterns. Minor observations include potential data loss risk from in-memory-only storage (non-blocking) and an optimization opportunity for frontend IPC calls (suggestion). The implementation correctly handles backward compatibility via #[serde(default)] for existing settings files.
